newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Doomed Democrats top opinion poll in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Doomed Democrats top opinion poll in Hong Kong.

text.p: Just four days before they are ousted by a China-appointed assembly, Hong Kong's democrats are riding high in public esteem -- much higher than the men and women who will replace them, an opinion poll showed on Friday.

The University of Hong Kong survey found activists like Martin Lee and Emily Lau, outspoken foes of Beijing's plans to stifle the territory's democratic aspirations, had far higher approval ratings than anyone else in the legislature.
"Classified by political background, members of the Democratic Party were the most popular among all existing legislative councillors," the University's Public Opinion Programme said in a statement.
Legislators were giving their final speeches to the Legislative Council on Friday, before the curtain falls on 156 years of British colonial rule and Hong Kong reverts to China on July 1.

The current legislature, elected in 1995 after Governor Chris Patten pushed through limited democratic reforms, is a mix of directly elected councillors, government-appointed representatives and members of the professions and of the business community.
China plans to disband the assembly and replace it with its own appointed Provisional Legislative Council.
Friday's opinion survey showed Democratic Party councillor Lau Chin-shek as the most popular politician with an average support rating of 63.7 percent.
Emily Lau of the Frontier Party (63.6 percent), Christine Loh of the Citizens' Party (62.7 percent) and Martin Lee of the Democrats (60.5 percent) followed closely behind.
Government-appointed members or representatives of the business community trailed far behind.
The pollsters questioned 538 people on June 23 and 24.
